newsitem.title: USA: First Bank System earnings fall in quarter.
newsitem.headline: First Bank System earnings fall in quarter.

text.p: First Bank System Inc. said Wednesday that earnings fell 5.6 percent in the third quarter due to a $51 million charge to pay an assessment to the federal agency that insures savings and loan deposits.

The Minneapolis-based bank, which failed in its bid to buy Los Angeles-based First Interstate Bancorp last year, said net income in the quarter fell to $137.5 million, or 99 cents a share, from $145.7 million, or $1.08 a share, in the 1995 quarter.

The results included the charge from the one-time assessment by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. on deposits at a savings and loan owned by First Bank. The FDIC is assessing savings and loans to bolster the Savings Association Insurance Fund, which insures thrift deposits.
Excluding the charge, equal to $31.6 million after taxes, operating earnings were $169.1 million, or $1.22 a share, in the quarter, a record, the bank said.
The strong operating results reflected growth in net interest and non-interest income, tight expense controls and effective capital management.
First Bank's stock fell 25 cents to $66.25 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
